title: Commas After Main and Subordinate Clauses

instruction.text: The text below is missing some commas. First, select all the coordinating conjunctions in the text.

atoms.b: Mandy is about to turn 45 ((so)) she is planning a big party. She is stressed about organising everything ((yet)) she knows the party will be great fun. Mandy will have a gold theme ((or)) she will have a pink theme. She went to the shop to look for balloons ((but)) all the pink balloons were sold out. Gold it was!

instruction.text: The text below is missing some commas. First, select all the coordinating conjunctions in the text.

atoms.b: Mandy didn’t expect many people to come ((nor)) did she expect many gifts. Nearly 25 guests came ((and)) everyone brought a gift with them! Mandy smiled all night long ((for)) this had been her best birthday ever.

instruction.text: The text below is missing some commas. First, select all the subordinating clauses and fronted adverbials in the text.

atoms.b: ((Despite the intense air conditioning)) the car was roasting hot. ((Even though it had only been two hours)) Mike felt like he had been driving all day. ((With the intention of having a short break)) Mike pulled into a car park and got out to stretch his legs.
atoms.sound: Despite the intense air conditioning, the car was roasting hot. Even though it had only been two hours, Mike felt like he had been driving all day. With the intention of having a short break, Mike pulled into a car park and got out to stretch his legs.
